Math labels (a TeX subset)

Source: R/math.R
tex.Rd

tex() builds a label from TeX math notation, for use anywhere an md() label goes: the label of text_grob(), vl_strwidth() and grobwidth(), and the titles, guides and text marks of vellumplot. vellum typesets it itself (no LaTeX installation, no web engine), with the sizes, shifts and glyph variants the font's OpenType MATH table specifies, so a formula renders the same in PNG, SVG and PDF and measures exactly what it draws.

Usage

tex(x, display = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A TeX math string, without $ delimiters (or a character vector, for one label per element). Or R's plotmath notation, unevaluated: a call or symbol (quote(x[i]^2), bquote()) or an expression vector (expression(alpha, beta), one label per element), translated to TeX as plotmath() describes.

display

TRUE sets the formula in TeX's display style (big operators larger, limits above and below, fractions full size); the default is inline text style.

Value

A vellum_tex_label (length-1 x) or a list of them.

Details

The formula is set in a math font, not in the label's fontfamily; the size comes from the grob's fontsize and every part takes the label's colour. The default font is STIX Two Math, bundled with vellum (SIL Open Font License, see system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "vellum")). Pick another with options(vellum.math_font = ): a family name known to systemfonts ("Latin Modern Math", "Cambria Math", "Fira Math") or a path to a font file. The font must have a MATH table.

Supported notation:

  • letters (set in math italic), digits, + - = < > ( ) [ ] , ; :

  • superscripts and subscripts, x^2, x_i, x_i^2, x^{a_b}, and primes f'

  • \frac{a}{b}, \dfrac, \tfrac, \binom{n}{k}, \sqrt{x}, \sqrt[n]{x}, and TeX's infix {a \over b}, {n \choose k} and {a \atop b}

  • Greek letters \alpha ... \omega, \Gamma ... \Omega, \varepsilon, \varphi, \vartheta, ...

  • operators and relations with TeX's spacing: \pm \mp \times \div \cdot \leq \geq \neq \approx \sim \equiv \propto \in \subset \cup \cap \to \Rightarrow \mapsto \infty \partial \nabla \forall \exists \ldots \cdots and more

  • big operators \sum \prod \int \oint and operator names \lim \max \min \sup \inf \log \exp \sin \cos \tan \ln (limits go above and below in display style; \limits / \nolimits override)

  • growing delimiters \left( ... \right), with [ ] \{ \} | \| \langle \rangle and the empty \left.; fixed sizes \big \Big \bigg \Bigg (and their l/r/m forms)

  • alphabets \mathrm \mathbf \mathit \mathbfit \boldsymbol \mathsf \mathtt \mathcal \mathbb, upright \text{...}, and \textit{}, \textbf{}, \textbfit{}

  • accents \hat \bar \tilde \vec \dot \ddot \mathring \widehat \overline \underline

  • \phantom{}, \hphantom{} and \vphantom{}: space with no ink

  • spacing \, \: \; \! \quad \qquad ~, and \displaystyle etc.

Scripts are placed with the font's italic correction and math kerning (cut-ins), as LuaTeX does. A label's box is baseline-stable: it is the line box a plain or [md()] label of the same fontfamily and fontsize gets, grown only where the formula reaches past it, so formulas set side by side share a baseline.

A command outside this subset is an error, not silently dropped, and so is nesting more than 100 levels deep. Characters the math font has no glyph for are drawn as its empty box, with a warning.

[ ]: R:%20 [ ]: R:%20 [md()]: R:md()

See also

md() for styled prose, which takes inline $...$ math; plotmath() for strings in R's plotmath notation.

Examples

lab <- tex("E = mc^2")
s <- vl_scene(3, 1.2) |>
  draw(text_grob(
    tex("\\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2", display = TRUE),
    gp = vl_gpar(fontsize = 16)
  ))
vl_strwidth(tex("\\frac{a}{b}"), fontsize = 12, unit = "pt")
#> [1] 7.9956
